- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5), model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is falling.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, reduce forecast by 5–10% in next 3–5 days.
- If model consistently forecasts below recent 10-day average, consider mean reversion bias — increase forecast toward historical mean.
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is volatile or mixed, model often overfits short-term noise; smooth forecast with 3–5 day moving average.
- If true outcome is significantly higher than model (e.g., >10% above), check if sentiment recently turned positive — model may have missed sentiment-driven rally.
- If model consistently underestimates during high sentiment + recent price uptrend, apply “sentiment multiplier” — add 0.1–0.3 to forecast if sentiment > 0.7.
- If model overestimates during low sentiment + recent price downtrend, apply “sentiment decay” — subtract 0.1–0.3 if sentiment < -0.3.
